title: Systems and State Functions Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A cup of tea with no lid, a closed steel tiffin and a flask that keeps tea hot all day. Each one lets a different thing escape. Aarav shuts his tiffin tight at 7 am, nothing gets out, yet his lunch is cold. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 5, Thermodynamics) we find out where the heat went.

You will see a chalk circle turn into a system, its surroundings, the boundary and the universe, then watch hot gas in three boxes on the molecule bench: open (matter and energy cross), closed (energy only) and isolated (neither, adiabatic walls). We describe a state with p, V, T and n, climb one hill by two paths to see why a state function cares only about the start and the end, while heat and work are path functions. Then extensive vs intensive properties, a worked example with two paths on a T-V graph, isothermal, isobaric, isochoric, adiabatic and cyclic processes, the exam trap, where it is asked, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 51 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Three containers, one puzzle
0:25 System, surroundings, boundary, universe
0:58 Open, closed and isolated systems
1:38 State functions: two paths up one hill
2:17 Extensive vs intensive (pause and think)
2:55 Worked example: two paths, same change
3:37 Five kinds of process
4:01 Exam trap and where it is asked
4:22 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:51 Recap and three questions
